config.title: Design Real-Time Dashboard

intro.title: Design Real-Time Dashboard
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a real-time dashboard component that displays live data updates, such as user count or sales metrics, in a React application. You will learn how to manage and update dynamic data using React's useState hook. The main technologies involved are React, TypeScript, and JSX for creating structured, type-safe UI components. This beginner-friendly project will help you understand how to handle state changes and render real-time information effectively.
intro.usecase: Real-time dashboards are essential in modern applications where live data monitoring drives decision-making. Developers implement these patterns in financial trading platforms that display stock price fluctuations, operations centers tracking delivery logistics, and social media analytics tools showing engagement metrics. These dashboards typically combine live data feeds with interactive charts, status indicators, and auto-refreshing components to provide immediate insights. Mastering this pattern prepares you to build monitoring tools, analytics interfaces, and any system requiring immediate data visualization.

objectives: Initialize and manage real-time data using React state hooks
Construct a responsive dashboard layout with a grid of components
Implement interactive UI controls to manipulate dashboard data
Render dynamic charts and metrics that update in real-time
Configure event handlers to simulate live data streaming
Integrate multiple dashboard widgets with shared state
Apply TypeScript interfaces to define and enforce data structures

steps.title: Import React and useState
steps.hint: Use the import statement to bring in React and the useState hook.
steps.analogousExample:
// Importing modules for a project
import React, { useState } from 'react';
steps.expectedOutcome: The imports are added at the top of the file.
successCriteria: React and useState are imported from 'react'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure to import both React and useState from 'react'.
steps.feedbackWrong: Check the import statement. You need to import React and useState from 'react'.

steps.title: Create Dashboard component
steps.instruction: Create a functional component named Dashboard that returns JSX. Use either a function declaration or arrow function syntax.
steps.hint: Define a component that returns a JSX element. For now, you can return a simple div or null.
steps.seedCode:
import React, { useState } from 'react';

// Create the Dashboard component here
steps.expectedOutcome: A Dashboard component is defined and ready to be used as the main component.
successCriteria: A functional component named Dashboard is created and returns JSX.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully created the Dashboard component.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure the component is named Dashboard and returns JSX.
steps.feedbackWrong: The Dashboard component is not correctly defined. Check the component name and return statement.

steps.title: Define interface for dashboard data
steps.instruction: Define a TypeScript interface named DashboardData with properties: activeUsers (number), totalSales (number), conversionRate (number), and revenue (number). Place this interface above your Dashboard component.
steps.hint: Use the 'interface' keyword followed by the interface name and property definitions. Each property should have a type annotation (e.g., activeUsers: number).
steps.expectedOutcome: You will have a DashboardData interface that types the dashboard metrics, enabling type safety for your component's state.
successCriteria: DashboardData interface is defined with all four required number properties.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've started defining the interface, but it's missing some required properties. Make sure to include all four: activeUsers, totalSales, conversionRate, and revenue - all typed as numbers.
steps.feedbackWrong: The interface definition is incorrect or missing. You need to create an interface named DashboardData with four number properties as specified.

steps.title: Initialize dashboard state
steps.instruction: Inside your Dashboard component, initialize a state variable named 'dashboardData' using useState, with the DashboardData type and default values.
steps.hint: Use the useState hook with your DashboardData interface to create state. Provide an initial object with default values matching the interface properties.
steps.expectedOutcome: The dashboardData state variable is initialized with default values matching the DashboardData interface.
successCriteria: dashboardData state is declared using useState with DashboardData type and initial object containing default values
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure you're using the DashboardData type with useState and providing default values.
steps.feedbackWrong: The state initialization is missing or incorrect. Use useState with DashboardData type and provide default values.

steps.title: Create update handler function
steps.instruction: Inside your Dashboard component, create a function named handleUpdateData that takes newData of type DashboardData and updates the dashboardData state with it.
steps.hint: Define a function that accepts a parameter and calls setDashboardData with that parameter.
steps.expectedOutcome: A handleUpdateData function that updates the dashboardData state when called with new data.
successCriteria: The handleUpdateData function is defined, accepts a DashboardData parameter, and calls setDashboardData with it.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've created a function, but make sure it accepts a DashboardData parameter and calls setDashboardData with it.
steps.feedbackWrong: The function is missing or doesn't properly update the state. Create handleUpdateData that takes newData and calls setDashboardData.

steps.title: Add main container structure
steps.instruction: In your Dashboard component, return a div element with the className 'dashboard-container' as the main container.
steps.hint: Replace the current return statement with a div that has the specified className.
steps.expectedOutcome: The Dashboard component now returns a div with className 'dashboard-container' as its main structure.
successCriteria: The component returns a div element with className 'dashboard-container'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've created the main container for the dashboard.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're returning a div with exactly className='dashboard-container'.
steps.feedbackWrong: Check that you've replaced the return statement with a div element having className 'dashboard-container'.

steps.title: Add dashboard header
steps.instruction: Inside the return statement of your Dashboard component, add an <h1> element with the text 'Real-Time Dashboard'.
steps.hint: Place the heading element directly inside the return statement. Use JSX syntax for the heading.
steps.expectedOutcome: The Dashboard component returns a single <h1> element containing the text 'Real-Time Dashboard'.
successCriteria: The return statement contains an <h1> element with the exact text 'Real-Time Dashboard'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you've added an <h1> element with exactly the text 'Real-Time Dashboard' in the return statement.
steps.feedbackWrong: The header element is missing or incorrect. Please add an <h1> element with the text 'Real-Time Dashboard' inside the return statement.

steps.title: Create metrics grid container
steps.instruction: Inside the Dashboard component's return statement, add a <div> element with className 'metrics-grid' directly after the existing header.
steps.hint: Place the new div element after the closing tag of the header. This will serve as the container for your metric cards.
steps.expectedOutcome: The Dashboard component now includes a metrics grid container element ready to hold metric cards.
successCriteria: A div element with className 'metrics-grid' is added after the header in the return statement.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you've added a div element with exactly className='metrics-grid' after the header.
steps.feedbackWrong: The metrics grid container hasn't been added correctly. Check that you've placed a div element with className 'metrics-grid' after the header.

steps.title: Display active users metric
steps.instruction: Inside the metrics grid container, add a div with className 'metric-card' that displays the activeUsers value from dashboardData. Use the format 'Active Users: {value}'.
steps.hint: Access dashboardData.activeUsers inside JSX curly braces. Remember to add the div inside the grid container you created earlier.
steps.expectedOutcome: A metric card displaying 'Active Users: ' followed by the activeUsers value from dashboardData appears in the metrics grid.
successCriteria: A div with className 'metric-card' exists inside the metrics-grid container
The div displays 'Active Users: ' followed by dashboardData.activeUsers
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure you're displaying the activeUsers value from dashboardData inside the metric card div.
steps.feedbackWrong: The metric card isn't displaying correctly. Check that you're accessing dashboardData.activeUsers and using the correct className.

steps.title: Add update button and wire handler
steps.instruction: Add a button element with the text 'Simulate Update' inside the metrics grid container and wire its onClick event to call the handleUpdateData function.
steps.hint: Place the button after the active users metric card. Use the onClick prop to call the handler function.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: button with click handler
<button onClick={handleClick}>Update Data</button>
steps.expectedOutcome: A button labeled 'Simulate Update' appears in the dashboard grid, and clicking it will trigger the data update handler.
successCriteria: Button element with text 'Simulate Update' is added to the metrics grid, and its onClick prop is set to handleUpdateData.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You added the button, but make sure it's properly wired to the handleUpdateData function using onClick.
steps.feedbackWrong: The button element is missing or not properly configured. Check that you've added a button with the correct text and onClick handler.
